title: HDFC Life Q4 results: Net profit rises 16% to Rs 477 crore, insurer declares Rs 2.1 dividend
summary: HDFC Life reported a 16% rise in Q4 net profit to Rs 477 crore and declared a final dividend of Rs 2.1 per share. Net premium income grew 16% to Rs 23,766 crore, VNB rose 11.5% to Rs 1,376 crore and solvency improved to 194%. APE increased 10% to Rs 5,186 crore. Record date for dividend is June 20, 2025.
content:
HDFC Life Insurance on April 17 reported a net profit of Rs 477 crore for the fourth quarter of FY25, up 16 percent from Rs 412 crore recorded in the year-ago period.

The insurer's net premium income for the quarter came in at Rs 23,766 crore, a 16 percent increase from Rs 20,488 crore in the year-ago quarter.

The company declared a final dividend of Rs 2.1 per share for FY25. The record date to determine shareholders' entitlement to the final dividend has been set as Friday, June 20, 2025, and the payment will be made on or after July 21, 2025.

HDFC Life's value of new business (VNB) rose by 11.5 percent year-over-year to Rs 1,376 crore in Q4, up from Rs 1,234 crore in the year-ago period. The solvency ratio of the insurer stood at 194 percent, compared with 187 percent a year earlier.

The company reported an annualised premium equivalent (APE) of Rs 5,186 crore for the quarter, a 10 percent increase from Rs 4,727 crore in the year-ago period. Individual APE for FY25 grew 18 percent, reflecting stronger retail momentum.

Shares of the insurer on the BSE closed trading at Rs 719 apiece on April 17, up 0.4 percent.

Vibha Padalkar, Managing Director and CEO of HDFC Life, said: "FY25 was a year where we deepened our reach, continued sharpening our value propositions and demonstrated the resilience of our business model. We are happy to report an 18% growth in Individual APE for FY25, in line with our stated growth aspirations for the year. Our overall industry market share expanded by 70 bps to 11.1% and by 30 bps to 15.7% within the private sector. Retail protection continued to show strong momentum with APE growth of 25%. All channels registered double-digit growth. We continue to enhance customer experience through intuitive digital platforms, with over 90% of service requests now handled via self-service."

She added: "As we enter our 25th year of existence, our aspiration remains, against a backdrop of a stable regulatory regime, to consistently outpace sector topline growth, deliver VNB growth in line with APE growth and double key metrics every 4 to 4.5 years."

The results highlight steady operational growth across sales, new business value and solvency metrics. The dividend declaration and improved VNB and solvency ratios are likely to be viewed positively by investors, while management commentary points to continued emphasis on digital servicing and retail protection as growth drivers.
